s: Which Biosphere Reserve became India's first high-altitude cold desert Biosphere Reserve in UNESCO's World Network of Biosphere Reserves in 2025?
x: The Cold Desert BR was added to the WNBR in 2025 as India's first high-altitude cold desert BR. Nilgiri (1986) was India's first BR, Nanda Devi followed in 1988, and Great Rann of Kutch is the largest.

s: In which year was the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve established?
x: Nilgiri was established in 1986, Nanda Devi in 1988, Gulf of Mannar in 1989 and Pachmarhi in 1999.

s: Which tiger reserve was declared a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve in 2020?
x: Panna Tiger Reserve was declared a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve in 2020.

s:
Arrange the following Biosphere Reserves in the order of their establishment, earliest first:
1. Pachmarhi
2. Nilgiri
3. Nokrek
4. Gulf of Mannar
x: Nilgiri (1986), Nokrek (1988), Gulf of Mannar (1989) and Pachmarhi (1999).

s: Which of the following Biosphere Reserves is not in UNESCO's World Network of Biosphere Reserves?
x: Kachchh, the largest Biosphere Reserve, is not in the World Network; Nilgiri (2000), Agasthyamalai (2016) and Khangchendzonga (2018) are.

s: Where does Nokrek, a national park and one of India's 1988 Biosphere Reserves, lie?
x: Nokrek is in the Garo Hills of Meghalaya, not the Khasi Hills or Manipur.

s: In which year was the Pachmarhi Biosphere Reserve established?
x: Pachmarhi was set up in 1999, after Nilgiri (1986), Nanda Devi and Nokrek (1988) and the 1989 group.

s: In which State is the Dibru-Saikhowa Biosphere Reserve, the smallest in India?
x: Dibru-Saikhowa (765 sq km), India's smallest biosphere reserve, is in Assam.

s: In which State is the Gulf of Mannar Biosphere Reserve?
x: The Gulf of Mannar BR (1989), India's second largest, lies off Tamil Nadu.

s: Which was the first Indian Biosphere Reserve to be included in UNESCO's World Network of Biosphere Reserves?
x: Nilgiri, India's first BR (1986), was also the first listed in UNESCO's World Network, in 2000.

s: Which one of the following is the correct order of the first, largest and smallest Biosphere Reserves of India?
o: Nilgiri; Great Rann of Kutch; Dibru-Saikhowa
Nilgiri; Dibru-Saikhowa; Great Rann of Kutch
Dibru-Saikhowa; Great Rann of Kutch; Nilgiri
Great Rann of Kutch; Nilgiri; Dibru-Saikhowa
x: Nilgiri was India’s first Biosphere Reserve, Great Rann of Kutch is the largest, and Dibru-Saikhowa is the smallest.

s: Jim Corbett National Park was originally established in 1936 under which name?
x: Jim Corbett National Park was established in 1936 as Hailey National Park and is recognised as India’s first national park.

s: According to the 2026 counts, how many National Parks and Wildlife Sanctuaries does India have respectively?
x: India has 109 National Parks and 573 Wildlife Sanctuaries (2026 counts); 127 is the number of Conservation Reserves.

s: According to the cited 29 July 2026 figure, Tiger Reserves span approximately what share of India’s area?
x: The cited figure states that Tiger Reserves span about 84,488 square kilometres, approximately 2.6 per cent of India’s area.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with its stated count?
x: The stated counts are 127 Conservation Reserves, 75 Community Reserves, 33 Elephant Reserves and 18 Biosphere Reserves.

s: India's protected area network covers about what share of the country's geographical area?
x: The PA network covers about 5.3% of India; national parks alone cover about 1.35% and tiger reserves about 2.6%.

s: After Madhya Pradesh, which State/UT has the most national parks?
x: Madhya Pradesh has the most national parks, followed by Andaman and Nicobar; Assam has 7.

s: How many Elephant Reserves does India have (2026)?
x: India has 33 Elephant Reserves; 18 is the count of Biosphere Reserves and 58 of Tiger Reserves.

s: Where is Tsarap Chu, India's largest high-altitude protected area, located?
x: Tsarap Chu is in Spiti, Himachal Pradesh. It is described as India's largest high-altitude protected area and Himachal Pradesh's fifth Conservation Reserve.

s: In which year was Corbett, India's first national park, established?
x: Corbett was set up in 1936 as Hailey National Park; Project Tiger was launched there in 1973.

s: India's first bird sanctuary is
x: Vedanthangal in Tamil Nadu is India's first bird sanctuary (PYQ 2024). Keoladeo is a national park and Ramsar site, Nelapattu is AP's smallest WLS, and Pitti is a bird sanctuary in Lakshadweep.

s: In which State is the Harike Wildlife Sanctuary located?
x: Harike is in Punjab; Sultanpur is in Haryana and Keoladeo at Bharatpur, Rajasthan.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Wild Ass Sanctuary – Little Rann of Kutch
x: The Wild Ass Sanctuary is in the Little Rann of Kutch. Narayan Sarovar is in Kutch, Harike at the Beas–Sutlej confluence, and Keoladeo is known for birds.

s: Daying Ering Wildlife Sanctuary is located in which State?
x: Daying Ering is in East Siang district, Arunachal Pradesh.

s: Where is the Wild Ass Sanctuary of Gujarat?
x: The Wild Ass Sanctuary is in the Little Rann of Kutch, Gujarat.

s: Mahuadanr Wildlife Sanctuary is located in Latehar district of which State?
x: Mahuadanr WLS is in Latehar, Jharkhand; Askot and Binsar are in Uttarakhand.

s: Binsar Wildlife Sanctuary is located in which district of Uttarakhand?
x: Binsar is in Almora; Askot is in Pithoragarh.

s: In which State is Sitanadi Wildlife Sanctuary, dominated by sal?
x: Sitanadi (553.36 sq km) is in Chhattisgarh and is mainly sal forest.

s: Khangchendzonga National Park was inscribed as a World Heritage Site in which year?
x: Khangchendzonga National Park in Sikkim was inscribed in 2016 and is a mixed World Heritage Site.

o: Great Himalayan National Park — Himachal Pradesh — 2014
x: The Western Ghats were inscribed as a natural World Heritage Site in 2012. s: The World Heritage property comprising Nanda Devi and Valley of Flowers National Parks was initially inscribed in:
x: Nanda Devi and Valley of Flowers National Parks were inscribed in 1988; the property was extended in 2005.

s: The Western Ghats were inscribed as a natural World Heritage Site in:
x: The Western Ghats, spread over six states, became a World Heritage Site in 2012.

s: Which of the following was inscribed as a natural World Heritage Site in 1987?
x: Sundarbans NP was inscribed in 1987; Kaziranga and Manas in 1985 and Great Himalayan NP in 2014.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about protected areas under the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972?
o: A Wildlife Sanctuary gives a higher degree of protection than a National Park
Grazing and private rights are not permitted in a National Park
A National Park provides the highest degree of protection among the categories
Some activities and rights may be regulated but allowed in a Wildlife Sanctuary
x: National Parks, not sanctuaries, provide the highest protection; sanctuaries allow some regulated activities and rights.

s: A Conservation Reserve under Section 36A of the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972, is generally established on:
o: Land located exclusively inside a National Park
Government-owned land adjoining or linking protected areas
Any urban land notified by a municipal body
Private land volunteered by a community
x: A Conservation Reserve is declared by the State on government-owned land next to or linking protected areas, after consultation with local people.

s: Who declares Conservation Reserves, in which local rights remain unaffected?
x: Conservation Reserves are declared by the State on government land; local rights are unaffected and panchayats sit on management committees.

s: A Community Reserve differs from a Conservation Reserve in that a Community Reserve is declared on:
o: Land acquired compulsorily by the Union Government
Private or community land voluntarily offered by the community
Wetlands situated within a National Park
Government land adjoining a National Park
x: A Community Reserve is established by the State on private or community land voluntarily offered by the community. Its rights remain unaffected, and the land cannot already be inside a National Park, Wildlife Sanctuary or Conservation Reserve.

s: Which recent judicially noted measure applies to wetland Conservation Reserves?
o: A 1-kilometre prohibition on all tourism activities
A complete ban on local rights
x: The Supreme Court extended a 10-kilometre mining buffer to all wetland Conservation Reserves. This is distinct from the ordinary 1-kilometre buffer around National Parks and Wildlife Sanctuaries.

s: On which date did the Wildlife Protection Act, India's first comprehensive wildlife law, receive Presidential assent?
x: The Wildlife Protection Act received Presidential assent on 9 September 1972.

s: What is the ordinary eco-sensitive buffer around national parks and wildlife sanctuaries?
x: The ordinary eco-sensitive buffer is 1 km; the 10-km mining buffer applies to wetland conservation reserves.

s: In which year did the Montreal Protocol enter into force?
x: The Montreal Protocol came into force in 1989.

s: Where is the Secretariat of the International Solar Alliance?
x: The ISA, launched at Paris in 2015, is the first treaty-based intergovernmental body headquartered in India, at Gurugram.

s: Banff National Park is located in which country and is associated with which mountain system?
x: Banff National Park is in Canada and is located in the Rocky Mountains. It was Canada’s first national park, established in 1885.

s: Which of the following statements about Yosemite National Park is incorrect?
o: Yosemite National Park is in the USA.
x: Option A is incorrect: Yosemite in the Sierra Nevada has granite cliffs and waterfalls, not mangroves.

s: Which of the following is NOT one of the 'Big Five' of Kruger National Park?
x: The Big Five are lion, leopard, elephant, rhinoceros and buffalo; the zebra is not one of them.

s: Which African wildlife area is an inland delta with high wildlife density?
x: The Okavango is the inland delta; Etosha is a salt pan and Virunga is known for mountain gorillas.

s: Galápagos National Park, the site of Darwin's study, is in:
x: The Galápagos, in Ecuador, have endemic species and were studied by Darwin.
